packet.headline_seed: In Caracas, this feels like the hardest moment in Venezuela's modern history
packet.description_seed: Rescue teams are working ceaselessly to reach those trapped under rubble. But as hope fades, anger is growing.

what: In Caracas, this feels like the hardest moment in Venezuela's modern history

clean_source_blocks.text: Rescue teams are working ceaselessly to reach those trapped under rubble. But as hope fades, anger is growing. Acting President Delcy Rodríguez says La Guaira has been hit hardest by the quakes. Hundreds are still feared trapped under the rubble, as families desperate for news. The 68-strong UK rescue team also includes firefighters from Cheshire, Lancashire and Greater Manchester. Video showing the aftermath of back-to-back earthquakes in Venezuela shows destruction on the capital's streets. Vanessa Silva visited the coastal state, where rescuers are still working to find survivors under the rubble after twin earthquakes rocked the country. The 68-strong team left Brize Norton airbase on Friday onboard an RAF plane carrying aid supplies. Héctor Bello wrote on social media that "you gave your own life for our daughter" in the quakes which killed at least 920 people.
Rescue teams are working ceaselessly to reach those trapped under rubble. But as hope fades, anger is growing.

In the same part of town, called Chacao, the Interim President, Delcy Rodriguez, took a tour with the mayor and was on the receiving end of residents' ire. "You're campaigning in the middle of a tragedy! The government isn't doing anything for the people," yelled one resident. On a personal level, I know these streets well. I lived in the affected neighbourhood of Los Palos Grandes in Chacao for several years when I was the BBC's Venezuela Correspondent. My old apartment block was just metres from the collapsed Petunia building, where rescue crews are working around the clock to reach trapped residents. A friend recently posted on social media that her mother was among the missing under the building's rubble.

It was a huge relief to see my old building, the Alheli, still intact and its genial caretaker, Pedro, still outside chatting to elderly residents on the porch. original_article.title: In Caracas, this feels like the hardest moment in Venezuela's modern history
original_article.description: Rescue teams are working ceaselessly to reach those trapped under rubble. But as hope fades, anger is growing.
original_article.research:
[Lähde: BBC World]
People sat with what remained of their belongings on the streets of the Venezuelan capital after homes were levelled by dual earthquakes

Each morning that Venezuelans wake to the aftermath of the dual earthquakes, it is a little darker, a little grimmer.

It means another night in which prayers for the miraculous recovery of missing loved ones went unanswered, in which the fitful sleep of the survivors is interrupted by nightmares of collapsed buildings and moments of sheer panic.

For ex-policeman Jan Carlos Roa Garcia and his family, it was another night sleeping rough. Their building in Caracas wasn't brought down but is too dangerous to return to.

Tears rolling down his cheeks, he says he's not sure he even knows how to rebuild his family's life again.

"If I was 30 and not 50, then maybe. But I don't know where to begin. And so far, no-one in authority has contacted us."

As a loyal public servant, Jan Carlos was careful not to over-criticise the government's response, exhausted and angry though he is.

Musician Zaira Castro had no such reservations.

"We're all pretty frustrated because the government is not showing what it should – a serious display of help," she says in a plaza just a block away from two collapsed buildings.

"It's actually us, the Venezuelans, who are helping each other. We live in a society that has grown into helping each other. We don't depend on the government – that doesn't exist for us anymore."

In the same part of town, called Chacao, the Interim President, Delcy Rodriguez, took a tour with the mayor and was on the receiving end of residents' ire.

"You're campaigning in the middle of a tragedy! The government isn't doing anything for the people," yelled one resident.

On a personal level, I know these streets well. I lived in the affected neighbourhood of Los Palos Grandes in Chacao for several years when I was the BBC's Venezuela Correspondent. My old apartment block was just metres from the collapsed Petunia building, where rescue crews are working around the clock to reach trapped residents. A friend recently posted on social media that her mother was among the missing under the building's rubble.

It was a huge relief to see my old building, the Alheli, still intact and its genial caretaker, Pedro, still outside chatting to elderly residents on the porch. One of them had twisted her ankle on the way down the building. All of them agreed they couldn't remember a tragedy this severe in Venezuela in their lives.

At th

---

[Lähde: BBC]
Rescue teams are working ceaselessly to reach those trapped under rubble. But as hope fades, anger is growing.

Acting President Delcy Rodríguez says La Guaira has been hit hardest by the quakes.

Hundreds are still feared trapped under the rubble, as families desperate for news.

The 68-strong UK rescue team also includes firefighters from Cheshire, Lancashire and Greater Manchester.

Video showing the aftermath of back-to-back earthquakes in Venezuela shows destruction on the capital's streets.

Vanessa Silva visited the coastal state, where rescuers are still working to find survivors under the rubble after twin earthquakes rocked the country.

The 68-strong team left Brize Norton airbase on Friday onboard an RAF plane carrying aid supplies.

Héctor Bello wrote on social media that "you gave your own life for our daughter" in the quakes which killed at least 920 people.

More than 900 people have been killed in the quakes and at least 3,360 others injured, according to officials.

payload.title: Venezuelan maanjäristysten tuhot koettelevat Caracasissa ja La Guairassa
payload.summary: Pelastustyöt jatkuvat Venezuelassa kahden peräkkäisen maanjäristyksen jälkeen, mutta toivo eloonjääneiden löytymisestä hiipuu ja asukkaiden viha viranomaisia kohtaan kasvaa.
payload.content:
Pelastustyöntekijät etsivät yhä raunioihin jääneitä Venezuelassa kahden peräkkäisen maanjäristyksen jälkeen. Tuhot näkyvät pääkaupunki Caracasin kaduilla, ja väliaikainen presidentti Delcy Rodríguez on sanonut La Guairan rannikko-osavaltion kärsineen järistyksistä pahimmin. Kuolleita on kerrottu olevan ainakin 920, ja satojen pelätään olevan edelleen loukussa sortuneiden rakennusten alla.

## Etsinnät jatkuvat raunioissa

Pelastajat ovat työskennelleet tauotta tavoittaakseen ihmisiä, joiden uskotaan olevan yhä betonin ja muun romun alla. Erityistä huomiota on saanut Caracasin Chacaossa sijaitseva Petunia-rakennus, jonka sortumapaikalla miehistöt ovat jatkaneet etsintöjä ympäri vuorokauden.

Perheet odottavat tietoja kadonneista omaisistaan, ja epävarmuus lisää painetta pelastustöiden edetessä. Yksi alueella asunut toimittaja kertoi ystävänsä julkaisseen sosiaalisessa mediassa, että tämän äiti oli kateissa rakennuksen raunioissa. Los Palos Grandesin kaupunginosassa sortunut Petunia sijaitsee vain muutaman metrin päässä Alheli-rakennuksesta, joka oli järistysten jälkeen yhä pystyssä.

Venezuelaan on lähtenyt myös 68-henkinen brittiläinen pelastusryhmä, johon kuuluu palomiehiä Cheshirestä, Lancashirestä ja Greater Manchesterista. Ryhmä lähti perjantaina Brize Nortonin lentotukikohdasta RAF:n koneella, joka kuljetti mukanaan avustustarvikkeita.

## Viha kasvaa viranomaisia kohtaan

Chacaossa viranomaisten vierailu herätti asukkaissa suuttumusta. Rodríguez kiersi aluetta pormestarin kanssa, mutta sai osakseen kovaa arvostelua. Yksi asukas syytti häntä kampanjoinnista tragedian keskellä ja huusi, ettei hallitus tee mitään ihmisten auttamiseksi.

Alueen asukkaiden kuvaukset kertovat sekä pelosta että helpotuksesta. Alheli-rakennuksen ulkopuolella sen talonmies Pedro keskusteli iäkkäiden asukkaiden kanssa kuistilla, ja yksi heistä oli nyrjäyttänyt nilkkansa poistuessaan rakennuksesta. Samalla läheisen Petunian raunioissa etsittiin yhä ihmisiä.

## Tragedian mittakaava järkyttää

Järistysten jälkeen julkaistut videot ovat näyttäneet tuhoa Caracasin kaduilla. Héctor Bello kirjoitti sosiaalisessa mediassa viestin, jossa hän sanoi toisen ihmisen antaneen oman henkensä hänen tyttärensä puolesta.

Alueella kohdatut asukkaat kuvasivat tapahtunutta poikkeuksellisen vakavaksi. Heidän mukaansa he eivät muistaneet Venezuelassa omana elinaikanaan yhtä ankaraa tragediaa. Pelastustöiden jatkuessa toivo eloonjääneiden löytymisestä hiipuu, mutta omaiset odottavat yhä tietoja raunioihin jääneistä.
summary_bullets: Venezuelassa etsitään yhä raunioihin jääneitä kahden peräkkäisen maanjäristyksen jälkeen.
Kuolleita on kerrottu olevan ainakin 920, ja satojen pelätään olevan edelleen loukussa.
Asukkaiden viha viranomaisia kohtaan on kasvanut etenkin Caracasin Chacaossa.
